title: The Best Nest
checkpoint: Reception Summer 1, week 3 — Phase 4: CCVCC words: two consonant sounds at the start and two at the end (no new sounds)
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 4 adds no new sounds. Instead it practises words with two or three consonants in a row, like nest, fast and strong. Encourage your child to say each sound and not skip one.

pages.illustration: Pip surveying a battered, half-collapsed nest in the ivy, one wing on his hip, assessing the damage. Twigs sticking out at wrong angles.
Flashback-feeling page: the same nest whole and perfect, neat and round and beautifully woven. Warm gold light. Show what was lost.
Nell flying in carrying a single twig longer than she is, wobbling badly under the weight. Comic and willing.

pages.text: They must not drop a twig.
pages.illustration: Close on two pairs of feet holding one twig very carefully between them, everything tense. Concentration on both faces.
The wind hitting: the ivy thrashing, twigs flying out of frame, both characters blown sideways. Chaotic diagonal energy.

pages.text: The nest fell in the sand.
pages.illustration: The nest landed upside down in a patch of sand at the foot of the wall, twigs scattered in a wide spray. Ground-level view.
Pip sitting alone beside the wreckage with his head down and shoulders low. Muted colours, lots of empty space. The sad page.
Nell beside him, one small leg on his wing, close-cropped and warm. Colour beginning to return to the page.

pages.text: We can fix it, said Nell.
pages.illustration: Both of them working, twigs in beaks and legs, the nest visibly re-forming between them. Busy and hopeful.

pages.text: The nest was strong and good.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the finished nest, rounder and sturdier than the original, with both of them sitting in it in the evening sun. Deeply satisfying.
